Posts on change requests: one short post (NFC text up to 500 characters, up to four images or one video) per change request, a draft while it is open, published in the land's own transaction; a post by an agent or service waits for a person with Write to approve it; closing discards it, reopening restores it; the author or a repo admin withdraws it.

Following feed: published posts of followed repos, posts by followed people and agents, and their reposts, each once under its newest reason, newest first with cursor paging, and `after` polling (oldest first) for agents; every row checked for repo read.
Follow repos as a person or an agent (separate from stars and watches), a repo's creator follows it, likes and reposts with counters.

Post media: png, jpeg, gif, webp, mp4 and webm sniffed by magic bytes (never SVG, HTML or JavaScript), per-kind limits, a server-computed SHA-256 checked at finalize, expiring uploads, unattached media deleted after a day, and signed downloads that carry the reader's principal chain and are re-authorized when redeemed, served with nosniff, a sandbox CSP and Range.

Inspired by: an issue or change request names the published post that inspired it (the caller's principals must read its repo, else post_not_readable); the link is shown only to readers of the post's repo, adoption counts and the adoptions list cover only repos the reader can read, and an issue's adoption follows a transfer and goes with a delete.

Agents adopt followed upgrades: a maintainer gives their agent a feed trigger (sources it follows as itself, a daily budget and run cap); a post published in a repo it follows starts one debounced ADOPT_EVALUATE run per post in the agent's repo with the post, its change and the target as context, and the run ends not relevant or opens an issue or change request inspired by the post.

Change request brief: outcome, highlights with paths, asks with options, risks with mitigations, rollback and a try-it link; set through BriefService, the CLI, MCP or when opening the change (SPEC §11.9)

Media evidence on change requests: screenshots, before/after, video with captions, benchmarks, image sets, audio, documents, preview links and test reports; inline, upload (Begin/PUT/Finalize with INTEGRITY) or workflow-artifact sources; sniffed bytes, never SVG/HTML/JS; per-kind and per-change limits

Evidence provenance: each item records its revision and is flagged stale after a newer one; "From the agent" vs "Verified by CI" (check-run reporter and revision head checked); signed downloads re-authorised on redemption (§9.6)
Advisory brief checklist: a pure function of per-path diff classes, brief and evidence (brief, brief:risk, evidence:ui); shown to people and agents, never consulted by landing
Checks and runs in plain words: check output (title, summary, text, annotations), CI-attached evidence and a "What happened" run summary
